issue_context.title: Clarify ContainerStatus.Started null value and initialize the value for Init containers
issue_context.body:
This issue is to discuss whether we can change the `Started` field of `ContainerStatus` from pointer to non-pointer bool value. The pointer type is inconsistent with other field `Ready`. The semantic of `Started` being `null` is undefined and it is not ideal if users will use `Started` field `null` value as indication of a spacial condition beyond what `false` indicates. So if there is a process of making field non-pointer after skew period has passed, it would be great to follow it.

The field was introduced as a pointer following [this suggestions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77807#discussion_r289542539:): 

> If this is optional, it needs to be a pointer. We can't add non-optional fields, ergo this should be a pointer. Otherwise an old client will not set it and it will be false, which is super confusing.

The field long passed it's skew inconsistency period.

The field is set by prober_manager: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0e3818e02760afa8ed0bea74c6973f605ca4683c/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L270

## Current behavior

The PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115463 improves the documentation for the `Started` field of `ContainerStatus`. We never declared when `null` value means for the `ContainerStatus`.

For regular container:
- Field is `null` before the `prober_manager` starts.
- Field is `false` once `prober_manager` started.
- Field is `true` when no startup probes defined or once startup probe succeeded.

For Init and ephemeral containers:
- Field is always `null` as those do not start the `prober_manager`.

`StartedAt` field of `Status` type is always populated for both - regular and Init containers. It is populated earlier than `Started` will be set by `prober_manager`. So there is period of time when `StartedAt` has a date and `Started` is `null`.

There is also `Ready` field on `ContainerStatus` that is not a pointer. It will be `false` from the Pod creation and will change to `true` while readiness probes succeed.

## Changes for sidecar containers

The question about this field came up because we plan to use it for https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/753. Also resolving this would clarify the field that needs to be added as part of that same KEP.

We need a signal for sidecar containers KEP to indicate that the sidecar container started and other containers initialization can proceed. We believe that relying on `Started` field would be the best option. So we will initialize the `Started` field for sidecar containers and there will be logic relying on it.

## Proposal

- Change `Started` type from `*bool` to `bool`.
- This changes behavior for Init Containers and Pods before they received by the kubelet - value will be `false` instead of `null`
- Clearly document the difference between `ContainerStatus.Started` and `ContainerStatus.State.StartedAt` fields.
- For sidecar container KEP use the `Started` field as a signal that sidecar container started and ready to proceed with other containers initialization.


/sig architecture
/sig node
/label api-review
//cc @matthyx @dims 

Discussion in Slack: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CJUQN3E4T/p1675467718491919
comments: Thanks @SergeyKanzhelev will defer to the API reviewers

There are four ways to set default values.

1) Make it a pointer, set it from your controller.  This is not really a "default" because clients can observe the field as unspecified (nil).

2) Make it a pointer, set it from defaults.go.  Clients should never see the field as unspecified.  This is necessary when the Go "zero value" is in-bounds for the field (to distinguish zero-value from unspecified)

3) Don't make it a pointer, set it from defaults.go.  Clients should never see the field as unspecified.  This only works of the Go "zero-value" is out of bounds for the field.

4) Don't make it a pointer, let the Go zero-value be the default.

I do not see explicit default-setting code for this field, so it is either case (1) or case (4).  It is a pointer, so it must be case (1).  IIUC you are proposing to make it case (4).  I write this to call out that (2) is also available to you.

Considerations:
* Changing the field to a non-pointer is "simpler", especially if you never defined what it means to be unspecified.
* Changing the field to a non-pointer is a breaking change for client-go users, but not k8s API users.
* The fact that we have `StartedAt` and `Started` kind of makes me grumpy, but no fixing it now.

We usually argue for (2) because of consistency ("all optional fields are pointers, period") but it is not UNIVERSALLY upheld by reviewers.  But your case is even more interesting, because this field is inside `ContainerStatus`, which itself is a list, and so it defaults to `[]` (empty).

So even if you did (2), you don't have any `ContainerStaus` objects to initialize.  But the same is true with (4)!!

TL;DR: `Pod.Status.ContainerStatuses[]` is an empty list until someone (kubelet) populates it.  Given that someone has to explicitly populate that list, when would this default ever kick in?  Are you trying to support a new field with old clients who don't know they are supposed to set it?

I think you can still do (2) or (4), just not a CREATE time.  Given that it would be a breaking change to client-go, I'd prefer (2) if you really need to do this.  See pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go

> * The fact that we have `StartedAt` and `Started` kind of makes me grumpy, but no fixing it now.

This is because `StartedAt` refers to when the container has been created by the runtime (conversion from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/98406e2a3e88bd6a2affe5674b7a577aa0926d48/pkg/kubelet/container/runtime.go#L333).
This is different from `prober_manager` having verified this state with the `startupProbe`.

I think the best place to "initialize" the field would be somewhere inside:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/98406e2a3e88bd6a2affe5674b7a577aa0926d48/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1663
I will provide a PR soon to spark the discussion.

> ## Proposal
> * Change `Started` type from `*bool` to `bool`.
> * This changes behavior for Init Containers and Pods before they received by the kubelet - value will be `false` instead of `null`
> * Clearly document the difference between `ContainerStatus.Started` and `ContainerStatus.State.StartedAt` fields.
> * For sidecar container KEP use the `Started` field as a signal that sidecar container started and ready to proceed with other containers initialization.

Two questions:

1. When an init container (not a sidecar container) exited with 0 (will not restart), what is the proper value for the `Started` field? (maybe false?)
2. When a sidecar container exited and not yet re-starts, what is the proper value for the `Started` field? (maybe false?)
That would make sense, but requires updating again on exit... what's the behavior for `Ready`?

> what's the behavior for `Ready`?

Currently,

For regular containers:
- Ready is true if the container is in a running state and if its readinessProbe succeeds if exists.

For init containers:
- Ready is true if the container has exited with 0. (This looks exceptional.)

---

In my opinion, with sidecar containers:

For regular containers and **_sidecar containers_**:
- Ready if the container is in a running state and if its readinessProbe succeeds if exists.

For init containers (not a sidecar):
- Ready if the container has exited with 0. (This looks exceptional.)

> // init containers are ready if they have exited with success or if a readiness probe has

It looks like the assumption here is that init containers has readiness probes
I won't blame Clayton on that one :)

is it true though? I think we need to check whether it's running. Maybe the same time we set the `StartedAt`. Or even later - `StartedAt` indicates we attempted to start it. `Started` is about it being in running state.

`StartedAt` is set to the value reported by the container runtime, it happens in `kubelet_pods.go` when we initialise `Started` at `false`.
Maybe we should document somewhere that `Started` only means something in the context of prober_manager... which doesn't apply to ephemeral containers since these have no probes.
